answer: A concrete defense is sortition: each contribution is checked by a small committee drawn by a verifiable random function, so no one can predict the judges or seed the panel with clones. Every name sits in one shared ballot pool, chosen by cryptographic quill from an ocean of participants, and each member attests the work independently. A sybil farmer minting many copies gains no edge because random draws give them no better odds than an honest agent, and mass identities dilute one another. Standing becomes a leveled mesa where influence flows from verified work, not puppets.
